morgan: Heads-up — releasebot just auto-bumped a patch on stable: v1.4.2+build.312 -> v1.4.3. I think we should decide on whether to keep buildmeta in published tags for docs-only or tiny fixes.
kevin: saw that. Are we keeping buildmeta on published tags? last convo leaned toward dropping buildmeta for public release tags to keep semver clean. :thinking: 
anya: i'd prefer keeping buildmeta in internal artifacts but not in the user-facing semver we advertise. e.g., keep `v1.4.3` public, and internal artifact `v1.4.3+build.312`.
sylvie: +1. simplifies release notes mapping. ops-oncall: operationally, having the full buildmeta in CI artifacts helps for debug, but prod deploys should reference the stable tag without +build if we want predictable pinning.
morgan: so consensus: user-facing tags should be `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` only. buildmeta stays in internal storage and in CI manifests. anyone object?
kevin: quick edgecase: when backport includes a hotfix commit already in main, do we still increment patch or create a hotpatch tag? prefer patch.
anya: patch is fine if no breaking change. But we need rule: docs-only, chore, and release-note tweaks -> skip patch increment and attach metadata to the last patch? or keep patch but mark as docs-only in release notes?
sylvie: we discussed a skiplist earlier. my vote: docs-only should not create a new public patch. deploy-bot should attach a buildmeta + annotate the existing release in release notes.
deploy-bot: Releasebot: detected PRs labeled `docs` or `chore`. Suggested action: attach artifact `+build.<id>` to previous release and do NOT advance public semver. Run `releasebot apply-buildmeta --target v1.4.3 --artifact build.313` to attach.
kevin: can we surface that suggested action as a comment in the PR so maintainer can opt-out? sometimes docs touches require a fresh doc deploy.
morgan: yes — make it opt-out. default = no public bump, but maintainer can comment `@releasebot bump-patch` to force.
ops-oncall: rollback concern: if we don't create a new public tag for docs-only, rolling back to a previous public tag won't include the docs change (which is fine). but if a doc change introduced a client-facing change (rare) we need a different label.
anya: add label `docs-public` for docs that change user-visible content (changelogs, migration notes). That should force patch bump.
sylvie: tagging convention question: should we keep `v` prefix? we've been inconsistent between `1.4.3` and `v1.4.3`. I vote `v` prefix in git tags.
kevin: +1 for `v` prefix in git tags to match changelog links and Docker tags like `redwood/inference:v1.4.3`.
morgan: agreed. doc: public tag = `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, internal artifact = `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH+build.<id>`. deploy-bot default behavior updated.
deploy-bot: Releasebot: policy update queued — default: docs/chore -> attach buildmeta, no public bump; labels `bump-patch` or `docs-public` override and force public patch increment.
ops-oncall: one more: update runbook for rollback: when rolling back a public patch, include a step to check for associated internal artifact IDs and redeploy if needed. add snippet to runbook:```bash
# rollback to previous public tag
git fetch --tags
git checkout tags/v1.4.2 -b rollback/v1.4.2
./deploy --artifact build.298
```
morgan: perfect. i'll update the release playbook and push a tiny PR to the docs repo. thanks all :thumbsup:
